questions.question: A resistor of $R = 100\ \Omega$ carries a current of $I = 2\ \mathrm{A}$. Find: (a) the power dissipated, (b) the heat generated in $t = 30\ \mathrm{s}$.
A $220\ \mathrm{V}$ electric heater has resistance $R = 484\ \Omega$. Find: (a) the current, (b) the power, (c) the cost of running it for $8\ \mathrm{hours}$ at $0.15\ \mathrm{JPY/kWh}$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $I = V/R = 220/484 = \dfrac{220}{484} = \dfrac{5}{11} \approx 0.455\ \mathrm{A}$

**(b)** $P = V^2/R = (220)^2/484 = 48400/484 = 100\ \mathrm{W}$

(Or $P = IV = 0.455 \times 220 = 100\ \mathrm{W}$ ✓)

**(c)** Energy = $P \times t = 0.1\ \mathrm{kW} \times 8\ \mathrm{h} = 0.8\ \mathrm{kWh}$

Cost = $0.8 \times 0.15 = 0.12\ \mathrm{JPY}$

questions.question: Derive all three equivalent forms of Joule heating power: $P = I^2R = V^2/R = IV$.
questions.answer:
**Starting from Ohm's Law:** $V = IR$

$P = IV$ (work done per unit time = voltage × current)

**Substitute $V = IR$:**

$P = I \times (IR) = I^2R$

**Substitute $I = V/R$:**

$P = \left(\dfrac{V}{R}\right) \times V = \dfrac{V^2}{R}$

**Summary:**
- $P = IV$: use when both $I$ and $V$ are known
- $P = I^2R$: use when $I$ and $R$ are known (independent of voltage)
- $P = V^2/R$: use when $V$ and $R$ are known (independent of current)

questions.question: Three resistors $R_1 = 6\ \Omega$, $R_2 = 3\ \Omega$, $R_3 = 2\ \Omega$ are in parallel, connected to a $12\ \mathrm{V}$ battery. Find: (a) the current through each, (b) the power dissipated in each, (c) the total power.
questions.answer:
In parallel: same voltage $V = 12\ \mathrm{V}$ across each.

**(a)** $I_1 = V/R_1 = 12/6 = 2\ \mathrm{A}$
$I_2 = 12/3 = 4\ \mathrm{A}$
$I_3 = 12/2 = 6\ \mathrm{A}$

**(b)** $P_1 = V^2/R_1 = 144/6 = 24\ \mathrm{W}$
$P_2 = 144/3 = 48\ \mathrm{W}$
$P_3 = 144/2 = 72\ \mathrm{W}$

**(c)** $P_{\text{total}} = 24 + 48 + 72 = 144\ \mathrm{W}$

Check: $R_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{1/6+1/3+1/2} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1\ \Omega$; $P = V^2/R_{\text{eq}} = 144/1 = 144\ \mathrm{W}$ ✓

questions.question: A wire has resistance $R = 0.5\ \Omega$ and carries $I = 100\ \mathrm{A}$ for $t = 1\ \mathrm{min}$. Find: (a) the power lost in the wire, (b) the heat generated.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $P = I^2R = (100)^2 \times 0.5 = 5000\ \mathrm{W} = 5\ \mathrm{kW}$

**(b)** $Q = Pt = 5000 \times 60 = 300{,}000\ \mathrm{J} = 300\ \mathrm{kJ}$

This illustrates why power transmission uses high voltage and low current — lower $I$ means much less $I^2R$ heating in transmission wires.

questions.question: A $60\ \mathrm{W}$ light bulb operates at $120\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) its resistance, (b) if the voltage drops to $108\ \mathrm{V}$ (10% drop), by what percentage does the power decrease?
questions.answer:
**(a)** $R = V^2/P = (120)^2/60 = 14400/60 = 240\ \Omega$

**(b)** $P = V^2/R$, so $P \propto V^2$:

$P' = (108)^2/240 = 11664/240 = 48.6\ \mathrm{W}$

Decrease: $\Delta P/P = (60 - 48.6)/60 = 11.4/60 \approx 19\%$

A 10% voltage drop causes nearly 19% power reduction (power drops as the **square** of voltage).

questions.question: In a series circuit with $R_1 = 4\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = 6\ \Omega$ connected to $V = 20\ \mathrm{V}$, find the power dissipated in each resistor.
questions.answer:
Series: $R_{\text{total}} = 4 + 6 = 10\ \Omega$

$I = V/R_{\text{total}} = 20/10 = 2\ \mathrm{A}$ (same through both)

$P_1 = I^2 R_1 = 4 \times 4 = 16\ \mathrm{W}$

$P_2 = I^2 R_2 = 4 \times 6 = 24\ \mathrm{W}$

$P_{\text{total}} = 16 + 24 = 40\ \mathrm{W}$

Check: $P = IV = 2 \times 20 = 40\ \mathrm{W}$ ✓

In series, power is distributed in proportion to resistance: $P_1/P_2 = R_1/R_2 = 4/6 = 2/3$.

questions.question: An electric kettle boils $m = 1\ \mathrm{kg}$ of water from $T_i = 20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $T_f = 100^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in $t = 4\ \mathrm{min}$. The kettle operates at $V = 220\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) the power required (assuming 100% efficiency), (b) the resistance of the heating element. ($c_w = 4200\ \mathrm{J/(kg\cdot K)}$)
A fuse rated at $I_{\max} = 5\ \mathrm{A}$ is in a circuit with $V = 240\ \mathrm{V}$. What is the maximum power the circuit can deliver before the fuse blows?
questions.answer:
$P_{\max} = V \times I_{\max} = 240 \times 5 = 1200\ \mathrm{W}$

The fuse blows if $P > 1200\ \mathrm{W}$.

If the load is resistive: $R_{\min} = V/I_{\max} = 240/5 = 48\ \Omega$ (minimum resistance that keeps the fuse intact).

questions.question: A resistor of $R = 50\ \Omega$ has a maximum power rating of $P_{\max} = 2\ \mathrm{W}$. Find: (a) the maximum current it can carry, (b) the maximum voltage across it.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $P = I^2R \Rightarrow I_{\max} = \sqrt{P_{\max}/R} = \sqrt{2/50} = \sqrt{0.04} = 0.2\ \mathrm{A}$

**(b)** $V_{\max} = I_{\max} R = 0.2 \times 50 = 10\ \mathrm{V}$

Or: $P = V^2/R \Rightarrow V_{\max} = \sqrt{P_{\max} R} = \sqrt{2 \times 50} = \sqrt{100} = 10\ \mathrm{V}$ ✓
